sections.heading: A delivery, heard across the home
text: A fictional capability story: one press can ring an indoor speaker, open a conversation, or play a saved reply. Audio is drawn silently; captions carry the words. Service routes are illustrative.

steps.text: The camera is watching the porch. No conversation or device sound has started.
The visitor presses the doorbell. Recording begins and the resident gets a notification.
The kitchen speaker announces the visitor. Sound comes from inside the home, while the doorbell keeps recording.

audio.text: Someone is at the front door.

steps.text: The resident opens the conversation. Video is available while the audio session connects.
The resident speaks into the phone; the same words leave the doorbell speaker. Video recording is unchanged.

audio.text: Please leave the package beside the blue door.
Please leave the package beside the blue door.
Please leave the package beside the blue door.

steps.text: The visitor replies. The camera captures their voice and the resident hears it through the phone.

audio.text: Of course. Have a good afternoon!
Of course. Have a good afternoon!
Of course. Have a good afternoon!

steps.text: The resident ends the call and the visitor leaves. The recording continues independently.
Quiet hours suppress the kitchen announcement. The phone notification and camera recording still exist.
No resident answers. A recorded reply is queued; the device has not spoken yet.

audio.text: Please leave your parcel by the door.
Please leave your parcel by the door.

steps.text: The doorbell plays the saved greeting. No homeowner or monitoring agent is talking live.

audio.text: Please leave your parcel by the door.
Please leave your parcel by the door.

steps.text: The phone cannot access its microphone. The resident can still hear the visitor, but no resident speech reaches the doorbell.

sections.heading: The operator has a voice
text: Watch the headset, the sound source at the house, and the visitor. Two-way audio, camera recording, spotlight control and emergency dispatch remain independent authored actions.

initial.detail: Armed away. Waiting for a reported event.
A sensor alarm alone does not assign a responder.

steps.text: The property is armed. The operator has not opened a camera or an audio session.
The camera reports a person at the door. Recording starts; the operator receives an event to assess.

monitor.detail: Person near the entry. Intent has not been established.

steps.text: The operator opens the camera feed and watches before intervening.
The operator opens two-way audio. No warning has played at the house yet.
The operator speaks into the headset. The warning comes out of the doorbell, with words anchored to the emitting device.

audio.text: This is the monitoring center. Please step away from the door.
This is the monitoring center. Please step away from the door.

steps.text: The visitor answers. The operator listens through the headset; the doorbell microphone captures the reply.

audio.text: Sorry, I have the wrong address.
Sorry, I have the wrong address.

steps.text: The visitor leaves. The operator closes the conversation; no responder is assigned.

monitor.detail: Visitor left after confirming the wrong address.

steps.text: In this alternate, the person stays and attempts the door. The operator reports a verified incident and explicitly switches on the spotlight.

monitor.detail: Operator observes an attempted entry in this authored branch.

steps.text: The operator requests a siren. The command is queued; the drawing shows no siren sound yet.

monitor.detail: Siren requested; activation is not yet confirmed.

steps.text: The device confirms the siren is sounding. The spotlight flashes, and recording remains active.
The operator requests emergency response as a separate action. The siren itself did not dispatch anyone.
Dispatch confirms a patrol unit is assigned and travelling to the house.
The patrol unit reports arrival. Resolution of the incident is not assumed.
The audio downlink fails before the warning reaches the camera. Video continues, but no sound leaves the doorbell.

audio.reason: Voice downlink interrupted; video remains available

audio.text: This is the monitoring center. Please step away from the door.

steps.text: The siren activation fails. The spotlight remains on; no siren animation or automatic dispatch appears.

monitor.detail: Siren unavailable. Operator must choose the next action.

sections.heading: Hearing an alarm is not detecting smoke
text: A sound source, a microphone, a classification and a notification are four separate events. This example uses an alarm test and makes no claim that there is a fire.

steps.text: An indoor camera records an empty room. No sound is classified.
The smoke alarm test emits a siren. Sound starts at that alarm, not at the camera.
The camera microphone picks up the sound. Classification has not happened yet.
The event is classified as a smoke-alarm sound and a notification is delivered. This does not establish that smoke or fire exists.

notify.title: Smoke alarm sound heard
notify.text: Indoor camera · sound classification, not a smoke measurement

steps.text: The camera heard a sound but cannot classify it as an alarm. It does not claim smoke or request emergency response.
